issue.title: DECISION: reconcile ledgers locally; full suite only at development → main promotion (root node)
issue.body:
## Decision (operator, 2026-10-17 PDT): ledgers reconcile locally; the full suite runs only at the development → main promotion boundary

**Status: DECIDED. Implementation and activation are separate approvals. This issue is the root node; link to it, do not re-argue it.**

### The decision

1. **Reconciliation is local by default.** After a PR lands on `development`, the ledger (releases.db, releases.sql, LEADERBOARD.md, RELEASES-PREVIEW.html, LEADERBOARD.html, CHANGELOG.md), receipts and PDDA bookkeeping are written by the landing session on the operator's machine, through the existing merge-cleanup Phase 5 path (`wave_reconcile.py`, `releases_app check`, `pdda.sh`). One writer at a time (same rule as the jog one-writer model, #1108).
2. **No routine full-suite run on development.** The hosted `wave-reconcile.yml` full qualification per merged PR is retired as a routine step. Development gets fast targeted checks (ci-route tiering, changed-area suites, containment/frozen-twin smoke).
3. **The full authoritative suite runs once, hosted, on the exact frozen candidate at development → main promotion**, with the macOS lane, sequential qualifying mode, and no blanket skips. Promotion blocks on it.
4. **No baseline-style benchmarks of the current system.** The old cadence is already measured (hosted ~49–70 min; local ~17 min; #1110). The operator will test the **new** cadence 2–3× once it exists. Nothing is re-run to re-measure what is known.
5. **Per-case approval for new CI tests stands.** Every new test case, assertion or parameter, even inside an existing suite, needs explicit operator approval.

### Why

- Batch #1124: one load-sensitive failure (gh610, 408/409) on a hosted reconcile cost ~2 h of serialized queue and would have blocked an unrelated merge. The second run was green. Re-qualifying every development merge on a single hosted lane is the bottleneck, not the code.
- The hosted lane is single-writer and serial by design; local reconcile removes queue time and the bookkeeping-commit retrigger loop (#1114).
- Cross-feature regressions that targeted checks miss surface at promotion instead, on a bounded batch, where one full run covers the combined result.

### Known costs (accepted)

- A laptop run is not a clean-environment witness (#991: 13 suites red locally from env leaks). Local reconcile writes bookkeeping; it does **not** claim qualification. Qualification is the promotion run.
- Catch-up discovery and the receipt contract currently expect hosted full receipts; until #1127 lands they will flag deferred qualification as missing. Transition rules live in #1127.
- Two sessions reconciling concurrently can race the ledger. Keep the one-writer rule; merge-cleanup already serializes through its attempt records under `.tick/merge-cleanup/`.

### Graph (children of this decision)

- #1127 — implementation proposal: promotion-boundary qualification, receipt/scope changes, catch-up, rollout and rollback. **The work item.**
- #1110 — CI audit that measured the cost.
- #1114 — stop bookkeeping commits re-triggering wave-reconcile (subsumed by local reconcile; keep for the parallel receipt-contract thread).
- #1118 — CI leaderboard decisions (parallel gate threshold: 2 of 2 clean back-to-back parallel runs, hosted macOS run, median parallel ≤ 40 % of sequential).
- #1124 — the batch where the cost was paid; carries the operator override comment.
- #1126 — gh610 determinism (root cause of the trigger failure; not blocked by, not blocking, this decision).
- #1130 — CI optimization umbrella (research only).
- #991 — local env-leak suites (why local ≠ qualification).
- #1125 / #1128 — hosted-reconcile attention alerts produced during the transition (close with a pointer here).

### Not decided here

- Parallel `validate.sh` as the qualifying form (governed by #1118's threshold and #1114's receipt contract).
- Any specific ci.yml / wave-reconcile.yml edit; branch protection and required-check wiring (inventory first, per #1127).

### Interim operating rule until #1127 lands

- Land PRs with merge-cleanup; let it reconcile locally. If the hosted wave-reconcile auto-fires, it may be cancelled by the operator; a cancelled hosted run is not a failure of the landing.
- Record every landing's local reconcile outcome on its merge-batch issue.
